Fig. 2. Guidance condition dominance varies across scenarios. The picture below defines the Bipartite Text condition. Specifically, the yellow region indicates erasure targets, whereas the blue region describes the scene after removal. Colored words specify target objects and associated physical effects. Row 1 necessitates a text-dominant configuration to effectively eliminate physical effects like ripples. Conversely, Row 2 requires a mask-dominant configuration to prevent erroneously removing non-target individuals. The proposed LD-CFG module effectively balances these modalities across diverse scenarios.

Fig. 5. Given the reference video, mask (yellow outline) and Bipartite Text, GenEraser successfully eliminates target objects and effects. Red and yellow text indicate the objects and effects to be removed, respectively.

Fig. 4. The two-stage training framework of GenEraser. During Stage I training, the MC-MoE mechanism randomly selects one of three branches for optimization to enhance model alignment with different conditions. During Stage II training, the LD-CFG module integrates features from three deterministic branches to balance textual and mask modalities. Finally, during the inference phase, only the output corresponding to the full guidance is utilized for the subsequent denoising process.
